definitions.definition: I={i∈ℤ:0≤i≤λ}. Factorials and binomial coefficients with indices in this range are those of the corresponding nonnegative integers.

definitions.type: family of complex linear endomorphisms of V indexed by nonnegative integers
definitions.definition: For each integer r≥0, X_r=x^r/r!, where powers denote composition of the action of x and X_0=Id_V.

definitions.type: family of complex linear endomorphisms of V indexed by nonnegative integers
definitions.definition: For each integer r≥0, Y_r=y^r/r!, where powers denote composition of the action of y and Y_0=Id_V.

definitions.type: subring of ℚ, also embedded in ℂ
definitions.definition: R=ℤ_(p)={a/b∈ℚ:a,b∈ℤ, b≠0, p does not divide b}, with the usual rational arithmetic and its embedding into ℂ.
M_R=R⊗_ℤ M. Once its multiplication map into V is proved injective, it is identified with its image in V.
ι_R is the tensor multiplication map determined by ι_R(r⊗m)=r m for r∈R and m∈M, using the rational scalar action on V.

definitions.type: K-vector space with induced lattice operators
definitions.definition: V(K)=M⊗_ℤ K. Every ℤ-linear operator on M acts by its tensor extension on V(K). The same symbols x,y,h,X_r,Y_r denote the tensor-induced actions of their restrictions to M once their preservation of M has been proved; this notation asserts no such preservation by itself.

L(K)=(ℤx+ℤy+ℤh)⊗_ℤ K, the scalar extension of the Chevalley ℤ-form with the commutator bracket inherited from sl₂(C). This is the Chevalley sl₂ construction also when the characteristic is 2. Its action on V(K) is induced from the actions on M.

inputs.statement: The integer map ℤ→K extends to ρ:R→K, ρ(a/d)=bar(a)/bar(d). There are natural K-linear isomorphisms V(K)=M⊗_ℤK ≃ M_R⊗_R K ≃ (M_R/pM_R)⊗_{ℱ_p}K, where ℱ_p=ℤ/pℤ acts on K by the prime-field embedding. V(K) has a K-basis β=(β_i)_{i∈I} of cardinality n>0, obtained from b e_i for a nonzero b∈J with J=Rb, and hence dim_K V(K)=n. The operators x,y,h and X_r,Y_r here are the tensor-induced lattice operators. The actions of x,y,h give the induced representation of the Chevalley ℤ-form tensored with K, and satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y, [x,y]=h on V(K). On β they and all the divided powers have the following integer matrices reduced to K: xβ_0=0, xβ_i=bar(λ-i+1)β_{i-1} for 1≤i≤λ; yβ_i=bar(i+1)β_{i+1} for i<λ, yβ_λ=0, hβ_i=bar(λ-2i)β_i; X_rβ_i=bar(binom(λ-i+r,r))β_{i-r} for r≤i and zero otherwise, Y_rβ_i=bar(binom(i+r,r))β_{i+r} for i+r≤λ and zero otherwise. For 0≤r≤λ, bar(r!)≠0, X_r=bar(r!)^{-1}x^r and Y_r=bar(r!)^{-1}y^r. For all i,j∈I the K-linear coordinate matrix unit T_ij relative to β is bar(binom(λ,j))^{-1}X_{λ-i}Y_λ X_λ Y_{λ-j}. Consequently every K-linear subspace of V(K) invariant under x,y is invariant under every T_ij.

inputs.statement: V=V(λ) is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(C)-module of highest weight λ, of complex dimension λ+1. The elements x,y,h are its Chevalley generators and satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y, [x,y]=h.

output.statement: V(K) is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊂V(K), if W is invariant under the induced operators x,y,h, then W={0} or W=V(K). Thus V(K) is an irreducible L(K)-module, including λ=0 and p=2, over the given arbitrary field K.

locals.type: K-basis of V(K) indexed by I
locals.declaration: Choose a basis β with all the matrix-unit and invariance properties asserted by N005.
Let W be an arbitrary K-linear subspace of V(K).
Choose a nonzero w∈W with its coordinates c and nonzero coordinate index j simultaneously from F001.
Choose the coordinate family c simultaneously with w and j as in F001.
Choose j∈I simultaneously with w,c from F001 so that c_j≠0.

locals.type: family of coordinate matrix units on β
locals.declaration: Let T_ij be the coordinate matrix units relative to β, as supplied by N005.

argument.text: H001 supplies the prime condition for the localized ring occurring in the input N005. N005 supplies β, a K-basis of V(K), of cardinality n>0. H003 gives 0∈I. Its member β_0 is nonzero since basis vectors are independent; hence V(K)≠0. Let W be arbitrary and temporarily assume L1: W is invariant under x,y,h. In particular it is invariant under x,y, and N005 therefore says it is invariant under every coordinate matrix unit on β. If W={0}, the required alternative already holds. For the other case temporarily assume L2: W≠{0}. There is a nonzero vector in W. Its expansion in β has a nonzero coordinate, since an expansion with all coordinates zero would be zero.

produces.statement: Under L1 and L2 there exist w0∈W and coefficients c0:I→K with w0=∑_{i∈I}c0_i β_i≠0 and an index j0∈I with c0_j0≠0; W is invariant under every coordinate matrix unit on β.

argument.text: Choose w,c,j from F001 within the nonzero branch. For every i∈I, applying the coordinate matrix unit T_ij gives T_ij w=c_j β_i∈W, since it kills all other basis coordinates and preserves W. Because c_j≠0 in the field K and W is K-linear, β_i=c_j^{-1}(c_j β_i) belongs to W. Thus every basis vector belongs to W, so its span, all of V(K), is contained in W. The reverse containment is part of W being a subspace of V(K). Hence W=V(K) in the nonzero case. Discharge L2; together with the zero case this proves W={0} or W=V(K) under L1. Discharge L1 into the antecedent to obtain F002.

produces.statement: If W is invariant under x,y,h then W={0} or W=V(K).

argument.text: Universal introduction over W proves the subspace assertion from F002, and F003 proves V(K)≠0. H004 gives the Chevalley bracket relations and hence closure of the integer span in D014. The action is the induced L(K)-action described in N005 and D014; invariance under its generators x,y,h is exactly invariance under their K-linear span, so this is irreducibility as an L(K)-module. No algebraic closure of K was used. At λ=0 the index set has one element and all relevant factorials and binomial coefficients are 1; all displayed arguments remain valid. At p=2 the allowed λ are 0 and 1 by H003; nothing used distinct reduced h-eigenvalues. These included endpoints satisfy the same conclusion.
